public_rationale: The rounded arithmetic is reproducible: 5.19% in year one, about $54.1 million monthly debt service, and approximately −40.28% under the stated subtraction method. That method subtracts depreciation and full debt payments together. It therefore does not establish the claimed gross margin. No independent same-model outcome source was found, and the speaker's own inputs cannot serve as independent confirmation under the evidence rules. This is not a finding that the arithmetic is uncheckable or that real data centers have these margins.
limitations: The hypothetical assumptions are not verified market prices or realized company results.
The arithmetic-only reading fares differently from the literal gross-margin reading.
The 8.87% cash residual is also hypothetical and excludes other cash uses.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: In the author's model, a debt-financed 100MW AI data center has a 5.19% first-year margin and roughly -40% once loan principal payments begin.

statement.excerpt: That’s a 5.19% gross margin, and you haven’t even started paying the principal. When that happens, you’re paying $54.1 million a month in loan payments, for a total of around $649 million a year for five more years, which comes out to around $1.48 billion, or a negative gross margin of around 40%.

from_speaker: around $649 million a year for five more years
our_interpretation: This is a check of the hypothetical model published on April 28, not an observation of a real company's realized finances.
The stated assumptions include $2.8 billion borrowed at 6%, a first year of interest-only payments, and repayment over the remaining 60 months.
I interpret the monthly payments as level payments with a monthly rate of 6% divided by 12 and no additional fees.
Arithmetic agreement and correct use of the term gross margin are separate questions.
The accounting basis is an author estimate. No GAAP, IFRS, or company-reported basis is claimed.
criteria.support_condition: Independent recalculation reproduces the rounded payments and percentages from the stated assumptions. Support for the literal gross-margin description additionally requires a coherent accounting treatment of depreciation, interest, and principal.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Recalculation produces materially different payments or percentages, or a same-model accounting reconciliation shows that the claimed gross margins result from mixing expenses with financing cash flows.
